en_nt_guide.text: {greeting} Welcome to Castle Coole, designed by James Wyatt for the first Earl Belmore and finished in 1798. It's one of the finest neoclassical houses in Ireland, if I say so myself, and I do, every day, at eleven and three.
The Portland stone came by ship from Dorset to Ballyshannon, by cart to Lough Erne, by barge across, and by cart again. That's why it cost a fortune. The Earl's son had to finish paying for it.
Upstairs there's a bed made up for King George IV, who visited Ireland in 1821. He never slept in it. It's still made up, just in case. Nobody wants to be caught out.
